title: Tabular foundation model flags cognitive impairment risk from questionnaire responses
summary: Using data from 45,604 older adults in five population-based ageing cohorts, a machine-learning pipeline built on a tabular foundation model used indicators of reduced survey response quality to identify cognitive impairment risk. The model jointly trained on the United States, England, India and Mexico outperformed country-specific models, with up to a 0.12 absolute AUC gain (about 20% relative) in an external validation cohort from China. Decision-curve analyses suggest population-level prioritization benefit; this is risk screening rather than diagnosis, and absolute AUCs are not stated in the abstract.
ai_technology: Tabular foundation model on questionnaire response-quality indicators

evidence.tested: Joint training across four cohorts and external validation in a Chinese cohort.
evidence.unknown: Absolute performance, diagnostic accuracy and prospective use; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A tabular foundation model predicted cognitive impairment risk from response behaviour.
